examples.ko: 창문에 철망이 달려 있어서 벌레가 안 들어와요.
examples.en: There is a wire mesh on the window, so bugs don't come in.
My grandfather fenced around the chicken coop with wire mesh.

examples.ko: 운동장 철망 너머로 공이 넘어가 버렸어요.
examples.en: The ball went over the wire fence at the playground.
I put the fish on a wire grill and grill it.
A cat stuck its face out through the wire mesh.

examples.ko: 낡은 철망에 구멍이 나서 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: There is a hole in the old wire mesh, so we need to fix it.

explain: 철사를 엮어 만든 그물 모양의 물건에 두루 쓰는 말이에요. '철조망'은 가시철사로 두른 울타리를 말할 때가 많아서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: This is a general word for things woven from wire in a net shape. '철조망' is often a fence made with barbed wire, so the two are different.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 있는 철문이 너무 무거워요.
examples.en: The iron gate in front of my house is too heavy.
This iron door only opens with a key.
I waited for my friend in front of the school's iron gate.
Please make sure to lock the iron gate at night.
If you go in through the iron door in the back alley, you'll find the shop.
Please don't lock your bike to the iron gate.

explain: '대문'은 집의 큰 문이고 '철문'은 쇠로 만든 문이라서, 쇠로 만든 대문을 철문이라고 부를 수 있어요. 무겁고 단단하고 차가운 느낌이 있어서 소리나 무게 이야기와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '대문' is a house's main gate, while '철문' describes a door made of iron, so an iron main gate can be called a 철문. It feels heavy, hard and cold, so it often comes up with talk of sound or weight.

examples.en: I needed nails, so I went to the hardware store.
The hardware store owner showed me how to use it.
I had a key copied at the neighborhood hardware store.
The hardware store closes at seven.
I'm looking for a hardware store to buy a light bulb.
Where is the nearest hardware store?

explain: 집을 고칠 때 쓰는 못, 망치, 전구 같은 작은 도구를 사거나 열쇠를 복사하러 가는 동네 가게예요. 큰 마트에서도 팔지만 필요한 걸 말하면 사장님이 골라 주는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: This is a neighborhood shop where you buy small tools like nails, hammers and bulbs, or get a key copied. Big supermarkets sell some of these too, but here the owner picks the right item when you describe what you need.

examples.en: Our team's defense is a real iron wall.

examples.ko: 철벽 수비 덕분에 한 골도 못 넣었어요.
examples.en: Because of their ironclad defense, we couldn't score a single goal.
The goalkeeper guarded the goal like a solid wall.

examples.ko: 그 건물은 철벽으로 둘러싸여 있어서 들어갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The building was surrounded by an iron wall, so I couldn't get in.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 철벽에 막혀서 점수를 못 냈어요.
examples.en: We were blocked by the other team's wall and couldn't score.

examples.ko: 철벽 같은 보안 덕분에 정보가 새지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the airtight security, no information leaked.

explain: '철벽 수비', '철벽 보안'처럼 뚫기 어려운 방어나 지키는 사람을 비유할 때 많이 써요. 요즘 대화에서는 다가오는 사람에게 틈을 안 주는 사람을 '철벽'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 소개팅에서 철벽을 쳐서 말도 못 붙였어요.
phrases.en: He put up a wall on the blind date, so I couldn't even talk to him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연애에서 다가오는 사람에게 선을 긋고 틈을 안 주는 모습을 가리키는 요즘 말이에요. 친구들끼리 가볍게 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modern slang expression for drawing a firm line and giving no opening to someone who is approaching you romantically. It's casual talk among friends.
phrases.en_equiv: put up a wall; shut someone down

explain_en: It is used figuratively for defenses or guards that are very hard to break through, as in '철벽 수비' and '철벽 보안'. In today's casual talk, a person who gives no opening to someone approaching them is also called '철벽'.

examples.en: I tried hanging from the bar at the park.

examples.ko: 철봉 운동을 하고 나서 팔이 아파요.
examples.en: My arms hurt after working out on the bar.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 철봉에서 턱걸이를 못 해요.
examples.en: I still can't do a pull-up on the bar.
The kids grabbed the bar and hung upside down.

examples.ko: 철봉이 높아서 아이가 손이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: The bar is high, so the child can't reach it.
I'm building arm strength with the bar.

explain: 놀이터나 공원, 학교 운동장에 있는 가로 막대예요. '철봉에 매달리다', '철봉 운동', '턱걸이'와 같이 자주 나와요. 체조 종목 이름으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is the horizontal bar found at playgrounds, parks and school fields. It often appears with '철봉에 매달리다', '철봉 운동' and '턱걸이' (pull-up). It is also the name of a gymnastics event.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 철없이 부모님께 화만 냈어요.
examples.en: When I was young, I just got angry at my parents without thinking.
Stop acting childishly and behave like an adult.
Back then I spent money recklessly, like a kid.

examples.ko: 동생이 철없이 웃는 모습을 보니 걱정돼요.
examples.en: Seeing my younger sibling laugh so carefree worries me.

examples.ko: 젊었을 때 철없이 한 말이 지금도 후회돼요.
examples.en: I still regret things I said thoughtlessly when I was young.

examples.ko: 철없이 행동한 걸 이제야 반성하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm only now reflecting on how immaturely I acted.

explain: '철이 없다'에서 나온 말이고, 반대는 '철이 들다'예요. 어린 사람에게도 쓰지만 어른이 생각 없이 행동할 때도 쓰고, 약간 나무라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The child has matured since starting school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이가 들면서 생각이 깊어지고 분별력이 생긴다는 뜻이에요. '철없다'와 짝으로 외워 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to gain good judgment and depth of thought as one grows. Learn it as a pair with '철없다'.

explain_en: It comes from '철이 없다', and the opposite is '철이 들다'. It can describe a child, but also an adult who acts without thinking, and it carries a slightly scolding tone.

examples.en: Korean spelling is often confusing.
I check the dictionary so I don't misspell things.
Spelling is easier in Korean than in English.
Spelling matters, but the content matters more.
I got a perfect score on the spelling test.

examples.ko: 영어 철자법 때문에 단어 외우기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: English spelling makes memorizing words hard.

explain: 글자를 어떻게 쓰는지에 관한 규칙이에요. 한국어 글쓰기에서는 보통 '맞춤법'이라고 많이 말하고, 영어 단어의 spelling을 이야기할 때 '철자'라는 말도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the rules for how words are written. For Korean writing people usually say '맞춤법', while '철자' is also common when talking about the spelling of English words.

examples.ko: 산 위에 높은 철탑이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A tall steel tower stands on top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 철탑 위에서 작업하는 분들이 대단해 보여요.
examples.en: The people who work on top of the pylon look amazing.

examples.ko: 철탑을 따라 전깃줄이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Power lines stretch long along the pylons.
I can see pylons lined up in the distance.
A bird built a nest on the tall steel tower.

examples.ko: 논 가운데 철탑 몇 개가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A few steel towers stand in the middle of the rice fields.

explain: 쇠 구조물로 만든 높은 탑이에요. 전깃줄을 걸어 놓은 송전 철탑을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 관광용 탑은 보통 '타워'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is a tall tower built from a steel structure, and often means a power transmission pylon holding up electric lines. Sightseeing towers are usually just called '타워'.

examples.ko: 영어 에세이 첨삭을 받고 나서 문장이 많이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After getting my English essay corrected, my sentences got a lot better.

examples.ko: 첨삭 결과에는 틀린 이유까지 적혀 있어서 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The correction results even say why things were wrong, so they help.
My teacher corrected my self-introduction for me.
I looked for mistakes while editing the writing myself.
I asked my friend to correct it for me.

examples.ko: 첨삭한 글을 다시 읽고 고쳐 썼어요.
examples.en: I reread the corrected piece and rewrote it.

explain: 주로 작문, 자기소개서, 보고서처럼 글을 선생님이나 전문가가 고쳐 주는 일에 써요. '첨삭을 받다', '첨삭해 주다' 형태로 자주 나오고, 그냥 '고치다'보다 설명과 조언이 같이 있는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when a teacher or expert fixes writing such as essays, self-introductions and reports. It often appears as '첨삭을 받다' or '첨삭해 주다', and feels like more than a plain '고치다' because explanations and advice usually come with it.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 노래로는 우리 학교에서 첫째가요.
examples.en: That friend is the best singer at our school.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 이 동네에서 맛으로 첫째간다고 소문났어요.
examples.en: That restaurant is rumored to be the best in this neighborhood for taste.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 수학 실력이 전국에서 첫째가는 학교예요.
examples.en: This is a school whose math skills are number one in the country.
The company that was once number one suddenly closed.
Kimchi stew can rank first in taste.
I practiced day and night to be number one.

explain: '첫째가는 + 명사'(예: 첫째가는 부자) 형태로 가장 많이 쓰고, 어떤 분야에서 가장 뛰어나다는 뜻이에요. '1등이다'보다 조금 글 같은 느낌이고, '둘째가라면 서럽다'는 이 말에서 나온 관용 표현이에요.

phrases.en: When it comes to singing, that friend would be upset to be called second.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에서 가장 뛰어나서 두 번째라고 하면 서러워할 정도일 때 써요. 그 사람이 최고라고 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used about someone so good at something that they would feel hurt to be called second best. It is praise saying that person is the best.

explain_en: It is most often used in the form '첫째가는 + noun' (e.g., 첫째가는 부자) to mean the best in some field. It sounds a bit more written than just saying '1등이다', and the idiom '둘째가라면 서럽다' is built on this word.

examples.en: I bought apples and pears at the produce store.

examples.ko: 새벽에 청과물 시장에 가서 물건을 떼어 와요.
examples.en: I go to the produce market at dawn to get goods.
The produce at this supermarket is really fresh.

examples.ko: 요즘 청과물 값이 올라서 장 보기가 부담돼요.
examples.en: Produce prices have gone up, so grocery shopping is a burden.
Mom went to the market to buy fruit and vegetables.

examples.ko: 채소와 과일 같은 청과물은 냉장고에 보관해요.
examples.en: I store produce like vegetables and fruit in the fridge.

explain: 채소와 과일을 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 대화에서는 '과일 가게', '채소 가게'라고 하는 때가 많고, 간판에서는 '○○청과'처럼 보일 때가 있어요.
explain_en: It is a single word covering both vegetables and fruit. In conversation people often say '과일 가게' or '채소 가게', and on shop signs you may see names like '○○청과'.

examples.en: At the sports day, our class is on the blue team.
Today the blue team won the tug of war.
We split into the blue and white teams and ran races.

examples.ko: 청군 응원 소리가 운동장에 울려 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The blue team's cheers rang out across the field.
I'm running in the relay as the blue team's representative.
The blue team wore blue headbands.

explain: 학교 운동회에서 반이나 학년을 둘로 나눌 때 파란색 쪽 팀을 부르는 말이에요. 짝말은 '백군'이고, '홍군'이 나올 때도 있어요.
explain_en: At school sports days, this is the name for the blue side when students are split into two teams. Its partner word is '백군' (white team), and sometimes '홍군' (red team) appears too.

examples.ko: 청년기에 겪은 경험이 평생 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Experiences in young adulthood affect you for life.
Most people worry a lot about their career path in young adulthood.
That writer spent his youth abroad.
Health habits from young adulthood carry into old age.
It's fascinating to hear stories of my grandfather's youth.

examples.ko: 청년기와 장년기는 몸 상태가 많이 달라요.
examples.en: Physical condition is very different in young adulthood and middle age.

explain: 사람의 삶을 나눌 때 '유아기, 청소년기, 청년기, 장년기, 노년기'처럼 나오는 시기 이름이에요. 청소년기 다음, 어른이 되어 가는 시기를 말해요. 글이나 수업에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: This is a life-stage name seen in lists like '유아기, 청소년기, 청년기, 장년기, 노년기'. It means the period after the teen years, when one becomes an adult. You often see it in texts and lessons.

examples.en: On hot summer days I crave a cold soft drink.

examples.ko: 청량음료를 너무 많이 마시면 이에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Drinking too much soda is bad for your teeth.
I bought popcorn and a soft drink at the cinema.
I like water better than soft drinks.
I got a can of soda from the vending machine.

examples.ko: 청량음료 대신 차를 마시는 건 어때요?
examples.en: How about drinking tea instead of soda?

explain: 콜라나 사이다처럼 시원하고 달콤한 음료를 두루 부르는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '탄산음료'나 '콜라, 사이다'처럼 말하는 때가 많고, '청량음료'는 설명이나 상품 소개에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is a general term for cool, sweet drinks like cola and cider (soda). In daily talk people often say '탄산음료' or name the drink, like '콜라' or '사이다', while '청량음료' shows up more in explanations and product descriptions.

examples.en: The traffic light turned green.
Cross the road only when the light is green.
This contract is a green light for the business.
My health checkup results came back with a green light.

examples.ko: 수출이 늘어난 건 회복의 청신호라고 봐요.
examples.en: I see the rise in exports as a good sign of recovery.
That news is practically a green light for the team.

explain: 교통 신호의 초록 불을 말하지만, 일이 잘 풀릴 것 같은 좋은 징조라는 비유로 더 자주 써요. 반대말은 '적신호'예요. 신호등 불은 말할 때 '파란불'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The new project has gotten the green light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 잘될 것 같다는 좋은 징조가 보일 때 써요. 반대는 '적신호가 켜지다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a good sign appears that something will go well. The opposite is '적신호가 켜지다'.

explain_en: It literally means the green traffic light, but it is used even more as a metaphor for a good sign that things will go well. The opposite is '적신호' (red light). In speech, the green traffic light is also called '파란불'.

examples.en: I was nervous before the exam, so I took a cheongsimhwan.

examples.ko: 청심환 한 알이면 마음이 좀 가라앉을까요?
examples.en: Would one cheongsimhwan pill calm me down a bit?
You can buy cheongsimhwan at a pharmacy.
The cheongsimhwan didn't make me sleepy.
I might take at least a cheongsimhwan before the presentation.
My grandmother believes cheongsimhwan works.

explain: 한방에서 온 환약으로, 긴장되거나 놀랐을 때 마음을 가라앉히려고 먹는 약으로 알려져 있어요. 시험, 면접, 발표 앞에서 '청심환 먹어야겠다'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 약이니까 먹기 전에 약사에게 물어보세요.
explain_en: It is a pill from traditional Korean medicine, known as something taken to calm nerves when anxious or startled. People joke '청심환 먹어야겠다' before exams, interviews or presentations. Since it is medicine, ask a pharmacist before taking it.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 청진기로 가슴 소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: The doctor listened to my chest with a stethoscope.
A nurse with a stethoscope around her neck walked by.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감 청진기를 귀에 대 봤어요.
examples.en: The child put a toy stethoscope to their ear.
The stethoscope felt cold and surprised me.
Medical students start by learning how to use a stethoscope.
I heard the stethoscope broke, so they bought a new one.

explain: 병원 장면에서 자주 나오는 단어예요. '청진기를 대다'처럼 쓰고, 이렇게 소리를 들으며 몸을 살피는 일은 '진찰'과 같이 연결해서 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: This word often appears in hospital scenes. It is used like '청진기를 대다' (to place a stethoscope), and it's easier to remember by linking it with '진찰' (medical examination).

examples.en: My older sister is a cellist who works in an orchestra.
I cried after hearing the cellist play.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 첼리스트가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, my dream was to become a cellist.

examples.ko: 그 첼리스트는 공연 때마다 같은 곡을 연주해요.
examples.en: That cellist plays the same piece at every concert.
I want to learn the cello from a cellist.
The cellists came on stage and took their seats.

explain: 악기 이름 뒤에 '-리스트/-니스트'가 붙은 직업 이름이에요. '바이올리니스트', '피아니스트'처럼 말해요. 악기는 '첼로'이고 '첼로 연주자'라고 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: This is a job name formed by adding a '-리스트/-니스트' ending to an instrument, like '바이올리니스트' and '피아니스트'. The instrument is '첼로', and you can also say '첼로 연주자' (cello player).

examples.en: The army charged into the enemy's castle.

examples.ko: 화가 난 손님이 가게 안으로 쳐들어가서 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: An angry customer barged into the shop and shouted.
Our team decided to charge into the enemy camp.

examples.ko: 아이들이 형 방으로 쳐들어가 장난을 쳤어요.
examples.en: The kids burst into their older brother's room and played pranks.

examples.ko: 경찰이 가게로 쳐들어가는 장면이 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: There's a scene in the movie where the police storm into a shop.

examples.ko: 게임에서 상대 기지로 쳐들어가야 이길 수 있어요.
examples.en: In the game you can only win by attacking the opponent's base.

explain: 그냥 '들어가다'와 달리 힘차게, 공격하듯이 안으로 들어가는 느낌이에요. 전쟁이나 게임뿐 아니라 화가 난 사람이 갑자기 들어갈 때도 써요. 반대로 들어오는 쪽에서 말하면 '쳐들어오다'예요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '들어가다', it feels like entering forcefully, like an attack. It is used for war and games, and also when an angry person bursts in. When seen from the side being entered, the word is '쳐들어오다'.

en: come to invade; come to attack

examples.en: The enemy suddenly attacked the castle.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 우리 집에 쳐들어와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A stranger barged into our house and I was shocked.

examples.ko: 화가 난 손님들이 가게로 쳐들어올까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried the angry customers might storm into the shop.

examples.ko: 친구들이 갑자기 쳐들어오는 바람에 청소를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My friends barged in suddenly, so I couldn't clean.

examples.ko: 게임에서 적이 우리 진영으로 쳐들어오고 있어요.
examples.en: In the game, the enemy is charging into our camp.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 이웃 나라가 쳐들어온 적이 있어요.
examples.en: A long time ago, a neighboring country invaded.

explain: 말하는 사람 쪽으로 힘차게 들어오는 것을 말해서 '쳐들어가다'와 방향이 반대예요. 전쟁뿐 아니라 갑자기 들이닥치는 사람에게도 써요. 딱딱한 말은 '침입하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes someone forcefully coming in toward the speaker, so its direction is the opposite of '쳐들어가다'. It is used for wars and also for people who suddenly burst in. The stiffer word is '침입하다'.

examples.ko: 중고 책을 비싸게 쳐줘서 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: I felt good because they gave me a high price for my used books.
The owner offered a generous price.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 오래돼서 값을 많이 못 쳐줘요.
examples.en: This bag is old, so I can't offer much for it.

examples.ko: 경력을 잘 쳐주는 회사에 취직하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work at a company that values experience well.

examples.ko: 돈을 좀 더 쳐주면 제가 팔게요.
examples.en: If you pay a bit more, I'll sell it.

examples.ko: 헌 차인데도 십만 원은 쳐준다고 했어요.
examples.en: They said they'd give 100,000 won even for an old car.

explain: '값을 쳐주다'처럼 값이나 경력과 함께 써서, 얼마만큼으로 계산해 주는지를 말해요. 돈 이야기에서 자주 나와서 '인정해 주다'보다 가격이나 대우의 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Used like '값을 쳐주다', it says how much something is counted as worth, and often goes with price or experience. Because it comes up in money talk, it feels more about price or treatment than the plain '인정해 주다' (to acknowledge).

examples.en: Jeon tastes good dipped in vinegar soy sauce.

examples.ko: 만두를 먹을 때 초간장을 같이 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me vinegar soy sauce when I eat dumplings.
Vinegar soy sauce is made by mixing vinegar into soy sauce.

examples.ko: 초간장 맛이 너무 새콤해서 물을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The vinegar soy sauce was too sour, so I added more water.
Vinegar soy sauce came out next to the pancake.
I seasoned cucumbers with homemade vinegar soy sauce.

explain: 간장에 식초를 섞은 찍어 먹는 소스예요. 전이나 만두처럼 기름진 음식과 잘 어울려요. 설탕, 물, 고춧가루를 넣는 집도 있어서 맛이 집마다 달라요.
explain_en: It is a dipping sauce made by mixing vinegar into soy sauce. It goes well with oily foods like jeon and dumplings. Some households add sugar, water or chili flakes, so the taste varies from home to home.

examples.ko: 친구가 영화 초대권 두 장을 줬어요.
examples.en: A friend gave me two movie invitation tickets.
I had an invitation ticket, so I saw the show for free.

examples.ko: 초대권 없이는 전시회에 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't get into the exhibition without an invitation ticket.

examples.ko: 이 초대권은 이번 주말까지만 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This invitation ticket can only be used until this weekend.

examples.ko: 회사에서 받은 초대권으로 가족과 함께 갔어요.
examples.en: I went with my family using the invitation ticket from my company.
I lost my invitation ticket, so I have to get another.

explain: 공연, 전시, 시사회 같은 행사에 초대받은 사람이 받는 표예요. '입장권'은 돈을 내고 사는 표도 포함하지만 '초대권'은 보통 무료로 받는 표예요. 짝말은 '초대권을 받다/주다/쓰다'예요.
explain_en: This is the ticket that an invited person receives for events like performances, exhibitions and previews. '입장권' (admission ticket) also includes tickets you pay for, while '초대권' is usually a free ticket. Common pairings are '초대권을 받다/주다/쓰다'.

examples.en: They say a super-sized typhoon is coming.

examples.ko: 우리 집 새 냉장고는 정말 초대형이에요.
examples.en: Our new fridge at home is truly huge.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 올해 초대형 프로젝트를 시작했어요.
examples.en: That company started a massive project this year.

examples.ko: 초대형으로 만든 풍선이 하늘에 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A balloon made in giant size is floating in the sky.

examples.ko: 작은 건 싸지만 초대형은 훨씬 비싸요.
examples.en: The small one is cheap, but the extra-large one is much pricier.

examples.ko: 초대형 피자 한 판을 넷이서 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: Four of us finished a whole super-sized pizza.

explain: '초-'가 붙어서 '대형'보다 훨씬 큰 것을 말해요. '소형, 중형, 대형, 초대형' 순서로 크기가 커져요. 태풍, 프로젝트, 화면처럼 규모가 큰 것 앞에 자주 붙어요.
explain_en: With the prefix '초-', it means much bigger than '대형' (large). Size goes up in the order '소형, 중형, 대형, 초대형'. It is often placed before things on a large scale, like typhoons, projects and screens.

examples.ko: 아이가 눈을 초롱초롱 빛내며 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: The child listens to the story with bright, sparkling eyes.
Stars twinkle clearly in the countryside night sky.
My puppy looked up at me with bright eyes.

examples.ko: 학생들이 초롱초롱 빛나는 눈으로 발표를 들었어요.
examples.en: The students listened to the presentation with sparkling eyes.

examples.ko: 잠을 푹 잤더니 눈이 초롱초롱 맑아요.
examples.en: After a good sleep, my eyes are bright and clear.

examples.ko: 아기가 초롱초롱 쳐다보는 얼굴을 보면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: Seeing the baby's face gazing up with bright eyes makes me smile.

explain: 주로 눈이나 별이 맑고 또렷하게 빛나는 모습에 써요. 같은 뿌리의 형용사가 '초롱초롱하다'예요. '반짝반짝'보다 맑고 정신이 또렷한 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for eyes or stars shining clear and bright. The adjective with the same root is '초롱초롱하다'. Compared with '반짝반짝', it gives a stronger sense of clearness and alertness.

examples.en: The child's eyes are so bright that they're adorable.
After a good sleep, my mind is wide awake.
I looked at the teacher with bright eyes.
All the students' eyes are so bright.
The night sky with sparkling stars is pretty.

examples.ko: 커피를 마셨더니 눈이 초롱초롱해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: After coffee my eyes are wide open and I can't sleep.

explain: 눈이 맑고 또렷할 때, 그리고 졸리지 않고 정신이 또렷할 때도 써요. 밤하늘의 별에도 쓸 수 있어요. 눈이 흐릿한 느낌의 '흐리멍덩하다'와 반대 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes eyes that are clear and bright, and also a mind that is awake and not sleepy. It can be used for stars in the night sky too. It feels opposite to '흐리멍덩하다', which means dull and hazy.

examples.en: Today is Chobok, so I ate samgyetang.
On Chobok I eat samgyetang with my family.
When Chobok comes, samgyetang restaurants are crowded.
When is Chobok this year?
The date of Chobok is different every year.
The sweltering dog days continue from Chobok to Malbok.

explain: 한여름 더위를 가리키는 '삼복'의 첫 번째 날이에요. 중복, 말복과 함께 '복날'이라고 해요. 이날 삼계탕 같은 보양식을 먹는 문화가 있어요.
explain_en: It is the first of the three hottest days of midsummer called '삼복'. Together with 중복 and 말복 they are called '복날'. There is a custom of eating energy-boosting food like samgyetang on these days.

examples.en: There is a big tree at the entrance of the village.
We decided to meet at the start of the alley.

examples.ko: 산길 초입까지는 버스로 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get to the start of the mountain trail by bus.
The entrance is narrow, so cars can't get in.
The beginning of this road is easy to walk.
The snack shop at the start of the market is delicious.

explain: 길, 골목, 마을, 산길 같은 곳이 시작되는 부분을 말해요. 문이 있는 '입구'와 달리 길이 시작되는 자리라는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 말로 '어귀'가 있어요.
explain_en: It means the starting part of a road, alley, village or mountain path. Unlike '입구', which suggests a door, it feels like the spot where a path begins. A similar word is '어귀'.

examples.en: The second hand of the clock keeps going round without stopping.

examples.ko: 초침 소리 때문에 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of the sound of the second hand.
I timed it while watching the second hand.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 초침 없이 조용히 움직여요.
examples.en: This clock moves quietly with no second hand.
It's the moment the second hand and minute hand overlap.
The second hand moves faster than the minute hand.

explain: 시계의 바늘 이름으로 '시침, 분침, 초침'을 같이 외워 두세요. 초침이 소리를 내는 시계 이야기에서 '초침 소리'라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Learn the clock hand names together: '시침' (hour hand), '분침' (minute hand) and '초침' (second hand). In talk about ticking clocks, the phrase '초침 소리' (sound of the second hand) comes up often.

examples.en: Fruit flies are flying around the fruit.
In summer, lots of fruit flies show up in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 초파리를 쫓으려고 식초를 컵에 담아 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put vinegar in a cup to get rid of the fruit flies.
Because of the fruit flies, I put the fruit in the fridge.
Fruit flies are very small.

examples.ko: 과일 주변에 초파리 몇 마리가 맴돌아요.
examples.en: A few fruit flies are hovering around the fruit.

explain: 과일이나 음식물 쓰레기 주변에 모이는 아주 작은 파리예요. 보통 파리나 모기와 달라서 따로 '초파리'라고 불러요. 과학 실험에도 쓰이는 곤충으로 알려져 있어요.
explain_en: It is a very small fly that gathers around fruit and food waste. It is different from the ordinary housefly and the mosquito, so it has its own name. It is also known as an insect used in science experiments.

en: the first day of a month

examples.en: On the first day of the lunar month, my grandmother goes to the temple.
Seollal is the first day of the first lunar month.
The first day of this month is a Monday.
From the new moon to the full moon, the moon gradually gets bigger.
When the first of the month comes, I hang a new calendar.
My grandmother goes to the temple on every first day and full moon day.

explain: 한 달의 첫째 날이에요. 일상에서는 '1일'이라고 하고, 음력 이야기나 명절, 전통 행사에서 자주 나와요. 짝으로 '보름'(15일), '그믐'(마지막 날)을 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It means the first day of a month. In everyday talk people just say '1일', while '초하루' often appears in talk about the lunar calendar, holidays and traditional events. Also learn the related words '보름' (the 15th) and '그믐' (the last day).

en: first-time trip on a road; unfamiliar road

examples.en: It was my first time on that road, so I turned on the navigation.
Driving on an unfamiliar road in the snow is scary.
Check the map beforehand when you travel an unfamiliar road.
Even though it was my first time, I found it easily thanks to the signs.
Walking a road for the first time, everything felt new.

examples.ko: 제가 초행길이라 잘 몰라요. 길 좀 알려 주시겠어요?
examples.en: It's my first time here, so I don't know it well. Could you show me the way?

explain: 처음 가 보는 길이나 낯선 곳으로 가는 길을 말해요. '초행길이라서 잘 몰라요'처럼 길을 모르는 이유를 말하거나 양해를 구할 때 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '낯선 길'이 있어요.
explain_en: It means a road you are traveling for the first time, or the way to an unfamiliar place. It is often used to explain why you don't know the way or to ask for understanding, as in '초행길이라서 잘 몰라요'. A similar phrase is '낯선 길' (unfamiliar road).

examples.en: The spring rain softly moistened the earth all night.

examples.ko: 피부를 촉촉이 유지하려고 물을 많이 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink a lot of water to keep my skin moist.
Morning dew formed softly on the blades of grass.

examples.ko: 빗속을 걷다 보니 머리가 촉촉이 젖었어요.
examples.en: After walking in the rain, my hair got damp.
My eyes grew moist while watching the movie.

examples.ko: 마른 화분에 물을 주어 흙을 촉촉이 적셨어요.
examples.en: I watered the dry flowerpot and moistened the soil.

explain: 조금 젖어서 부드럽고 눈에 띄게 습기가 있는 모양을 말해요. '적시다, 젖다, 맺히다' 같은 동사와 같이 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '촉촉하게'도 같은 뜻으로 자연스럽게 써요.
explain_en: It describes something lightly wet, soft and visibly damp. It often appears with verbs like '적시다', '젖다' and '맺히다'. In speech, '촉촉하게' is also a natural way to say the same thing.
